root_cause.text: retry_aligned_read() in md/raid5 released an overlapped stripe through the lockless released_stripes path, allowing find_get_stripe() to remove that stripe from handle_list before handle_stripe() ran, so the stripe was never processed to clear the overlap and raid5d looped indefinitely.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that raid5_release_stripe() put the stripe on released_stripes, release_stripe_list() later moved it to handle_list because STRIPE_HANDLE was set, and then retry_aligned_read() removed it via find_get_stripe() -> list_del_init(), "prevent[ing] handle_stripe() from ever processing the stripe"; the patch replaces raid5_release_stripe(sh) with __release_stripe(conf, sh, &conf->temp_inactive_list[hash]) to avoid that path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix aligned-read retry failure handling by releasing the stripe under device_lock to the proper temp inactive hash list instead of using the generic stripe release helper.
intent_record.what: In the failure path when add_stripe_bio(sh, raid_bio, dd_idx, 0, 0) returns false inside retry_aligned_read(), the code replaces a call to raid5_release_stripe(sh) with an explicit locked release sequence: it declares a local hash variable, takes conf->device_lock with spin_lock_irq(), reads sh->hash_lock_index into hash, calls __release_stripe(conf, sh, &conf->temp_inactive_list[hash]), and then unlocks with spin_unlock_irq().
intent_record.how: At runtime, when attaching the bio to the stripe fails during aligned read retry handling, the stripe is now released under the RAID device lock onto the specific temp_inactive_list bucket associated with the stripe's hash index instead of using the generic release helper. This changes the failure-path cleanup to use the correct internal release mechanism and list placement, helping avoid incorrect stripe state handling or races during retry setup.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the aligned-read retry path in raid5 by avoiding the generic lockless stripe release and instead releasing under device_lock to the correct inactive list, which addresses the root cause where retry_aligned_read() could release an overlapped stripe in a way that let it be removed from handle_list before handle_stripe() cleared the overlap.
